findings.issue_text: Sibling-domain heuristic in user_serializer.rb (elsif branch, lines 145-147) produces false positives on two-label public suffixes (ccTLDs): when the shared tail is a public suffix like .com.au or .co.uk rather than a registrable domain, unrelated third-party sites match (e.g., discourse.com.au vs other.com.au both strip to 'com.au'), causing the full path of a completely unrelated site to be displayed as website_name

Website-on-child-subdomain of the instance matches no branch, creating asymmetry with the parent case: instance example.com with website www.example.com falls through all branches (label counts 3 vs 2 fail the elsif, ends_with? check fails) and shows host-only name, while the mirror case (instance www.example.com, website example.com) shows the path; deeper siblings like a.b.example.com vs x.b.example.com also never match since only the first label is stripped

Present-but-unparseable website URLs hide the website row entirely due to guard/value mismatch: include_website_name keys off website.present? but website_name can return nil when URI() raises (URLs with spaces, non-ASCII/IDN hosts) or when the URI has no host, resulting in website_name: null that hides the entire website row, and the rescue nil silently masks the parse failure rather than degrading to displaying the host

Same-domain detection never fires when the website host is a subdomain (child) of the instance host: in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141-149, the website_name branches handle exact host equality, sibling subdomains with equal label counts, and the website host being a parent of the instance host, but there is no branch for the website host being a child of the instance host (e.g., website 'www.example.com/t/123' on an instance at 'example.com' falls to the else, 'example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com') is false, and only the bare host 'www.example.com' is returned with the path dropped). The else branch needs the symmetric check (website_host.ends_with?('.' << discourse_host)) or a restructured comparison, so the feature silently no-ops in one of the most common real configurations.

include_website_name guard doesn't match the computed value, causing 'website_name': null to be serialized and the website row to silently disappear: include_website_name (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153) gates on website.present?, but website_name returns nil whenever URI(website.to_s) yields no host (unparseable values where rescue nil swallows URI::InvalidURIError for URLs with spaces/non-ASCII/invalid encoding, hostless schemes like 'mailto:foo@bar.com', and scheme-less values like 'example.com/path'), so the payload contains an explicit null and the template's {{#if model.website_name}} (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66) hides the website entirely. This is also a regression versus the removed frontend code for inputs like 'http://foo bar.com/x' or 'http://例え.jp' that the old website.split("/")[2] still displayed; the guard should reflect the computed result (e.g., website_name.present?), and no spec covers the unparseable/hostless nil path.

The `elsif` branch of `website_name` (the sibling-subdomain case: equal label count and > 2 labels, e.g. website `www.example.com` on instance `forum.example.com`) is never exercised by any test for either its true or false outcome, so a future refactor breaking the label comparison or the `> 2` guard would pass CI silently

The frontend behavioral change ships with zero frontend test work: nothing verifies the profile actually renders `model.website_name` (presence gating, `href`, `rel=nofollow` via `removeNoFollow`, `target=_blank`), so serializer specs cannot catch a template/controller wiring mistake such as a wrong property name or a payload path missing the attribute
The `websiteName` computed property is deleted from the user controller, but there is no evidence existing QUnit/acceptance tests referencing it or the profile website display were updated or removed
The degradation path where the serializer omits `website_name` and the website silently disappears from profiles has no acceptance test to catch the regression
No test verifies `website_name` is omitted/nil when `website` is blank; if `include_website_name` regressed to always-true, no test would fail
No test verifies `website_name` returns nil when `website` is present but unparseable (the `rescue nil` path), which serializes as `website_name: null` alongside a present `website`

Path edge cases are unpinned: `URI('http://example.com').path` is `""` while `URI('http://example.com/').path` is `"/"`, so a same-domain website renders as `example.com` vs `example.com/` — a visible change from the old host-only display — and neither input is tested
Query strings/fragments (e.g. `?a=b`) are silently dropped from the displayed website name with no test documenting that intent

Dead conditional-inclusion guard: the new `include_website_name` method (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:154) is never invoked because ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8.x dispatches conditional attribute inclusion via `include_#{attribute}?` with a trailing question mark, so `website_name` is emitted unconditionally (as null for every user without a website); the new specs only serialize users with a website, so the suite passes whether the gate works or not and nothing in CI can detect the inert guard — the method should be renamed to `include_website_name?` and a spec added asserting the json has no `:website_name` key when the website is blank.

The `rescue nil` fallback at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:139 silently hides the website entirely for stored website values that strict URI parsing rejects (e.g. `http://example.com/my page`, URLs with non-ASCII characters or `|`): the old client-side code (`website.split("/")[2]`) still displayed the host for such values, but the new backend returns nil and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` renders nothing — a silent regression where the failure mode should be "show host", not "show nothing".

The domain-matching heuristic at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145-150 silently no-ops for common same-site cases: on a two-label instance domain (e.g. example.com), a website at `www.example.com/blog` or `blog.example.com/post` matches no branch (the elsif requires equal label counts, the else only matches when the website host is a dot-suffixed parent of the instance host), and sibling subdomains with differing label counts also fall through; additionally, the elsif branch — the most convoluted logic in the method — is the only branch with zero spec coverage, so future edits there are invisible to CI.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sibling-domain heuristic in user_serializer.rb (elsif branch, lines 145-147) produces false positives on two-label public suffixes (ccTLDs): when the shared tail is a public suffix like .com.au or .co.uk rather than a registrable domain, unrelated third-party sites match (e.g., discourse.com.au vs other.com.au both strip to 'com.au'), causing the full path of a completely unrelated site to be displayed as website_name

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `elsif` branch treats domains with the same label count (>2) as “siblings” by comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')` to the same slice of `discourse_host`. For ccTLD-style public suffixes like `com.au`/`co.uk`, unrelated hosts such as `discourse.com.au` and `other.com.au` both reduce to `com.au`, so the condition becomes true and returns `website_host + path`, incorrectly displaying a full path for an unrelated site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Website-on-child-subdomain of the instance matches no branch, creating asymmetry with the parent case: instance example.com with website www.example.com falls through all branches (label counts 3 vs 2 fail the elsif, ends_with? check fails) and shows host-only name, while the mirror case (instance www.example.com, website example.com) shows the path; deeper siblings like a.b.example.com vs x.b.example.com also never match since only the first label is stripped

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “path included” cases only cover exact host match, sibling subdomains with the same label count (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), and when the *instance* is a child of the website host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)`). For the reverse (instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com`), none of those branches match and it returns only `website_host` (no path), while the mirror case (instance `www.example.com`, website `example.com`) does include the path. That asymmetry is visible from the code and may be an unhandled edge-case rather than a clear defect. However, the finding’s claim that deeper siblings like `a.b.example.com` vs `x.b.example.com` “never match” is incorrect: the `elsif` branch *would* match those (same label count > 2, and stripping the first label makes both `b.example.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Present-but-unparseable website URLs hide the website row entirely due to guard/value mismatch: include_website_name keys off website.present? but website_name can return nil when URI() raises (URLs with spaces, non-ASCII/IDN hosts) or when the URI has no host, resulting in website_name: null that hides the entire website row, and the rescue nil silently masks the parse failure rather than degrading to displaying the host

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `include_website_name` returns `website.present?`, but `website_name` can return `nil` because it does `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and immediately `return if website_host.nil?`. The template was changed to render the website only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so a present-but-unparseable/hostless `website` (e.g., missing scheme, invalid URI) will result in `website_name: null` and the website display will be omitted despite `website` being set. The `rescue nil` also silently masks parse failures instead of degrading to a displayable value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same-domain detection never fires when the website host is a subdomain (child) of the instance host: in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141-149, the website_name branches handle exact host equality, sibling subdomains with equal label counts, and the website host being a parent of the instance host, but there is no branch for the website host being a child of the instance host (e.g., website 'www.example.com/t/123' on an instance at 'example.com' falls to the else, 'example.com'.ends_with?('.www.example.com') is false, and only the bare host 'www.example.com' is returned with the path dropped). The else branch needs the symmetric check (website_host.ends_with?('.' << discourse_host)) or a restructured comparison, so the feature silently no-ops in one of the most common real configurations.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the logic includes the URL path only for (1) exact host match (`website_host == discourse_host`), (2) “sibling” subdomains with equal label counts, or (3) when the instance host is a subdomain of the website host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`). There is no symmetric check for the website host being a subdomain of the instance host (e.g., `website_host = www.example.com`, `discourse_host = example.com`), so that case will fall through and return only `website_host` without the path. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case gap, but it does not clearly constitute a verifiable defect/regression because the previous client-side behavior always dropped the path anyway (it only displayed the host).

adjudication_records.issue_text: include_website_name guard doesn't match the computed value, causing 'website_name': null to be serialized and the website row to silently disappear: include_website_name (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153) gates on website.present?, but website_name returns nil whenever URI(website.to_s) yields no host (unparseable values where rescue nil swallows URI::InvalidURIError for URLs with spaces/non-ASCII/invalid encoding, hostless schemes like 'mailto:foo@bar.com', and scheme-less values like 'example.com/path'), so the payload contains an explicit null and the template's {{#if model.website_name}} (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66) hides the website entirely. This is also a regression versus the removed frontend code for inputs like 'http://foo bar.com/x' or 'http://例え.jp' that the old website.split("/")[2] still displayed; the guard should reflect the computed result (e.g., website_name.present?), and no spec covers the unparseable/hostless nil path.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `include_website_name` (user_serializer.rb) only checks `website.present?`, while `website_name` can return `nil` when `URI(website.to_s).host` is `nil` (it explicitly `return`s if `website_host.nil?` and also rescues parse errors to `nil`). The template was changed to render the website row only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), so any case where `website` is present but `website_name` computes to `nil` would hide the website display. However, the diff does not show whether such “unparseable/hostless” website values are actually permitted by validations, so the claim of an actual regression/bug for real user inputs isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone; it is a concrete edge-case/guard mismatch and the specs added don’t cover the nil/parse-failure path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `elsif` branch of `website_name` (the sibling-subdomain case: equal label count and > 2 labels, e.g. website `www.example.com` on instance `forum.example.com`) is never exercised by any test for either its true or false outcome, so a future refactor breaking the label comparison or the `> 2` guard would pass CI silently

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch is only reachable when both hosts have the same number of dot-labels and that count is > 2 (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). The added specs exercise the `if website_host == discourse_host` case (`example.com`), and the final `else` case for unrelated domains (`discourse.org`) and parent-domain (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`), but none sets `website_host` to a 3+ label host matching the instance label count. So neither outcome of the ternary inside that `elsif` is covered, meaning refactors to the label-count guard or sibling-subdomain comparison could slip through CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The frontend behavioral change ships with zero frontend test work: nothing verifies the profile actually renders `model.website_name` (presence gating, `href`, `rel=nofollow` via `removeNoFollow`, `target=_blank`), so serializer specs cannot catch a template/controller wiring mistake such as a wrong property name or a payload path missing the attribute

adjudication.rationale: Diff changes the frontend template from `websiteName` (a controller computed) to `model.website_name` (`user/user.hbs`), and removes the controller property entirely (`controllers/user.js.es6`). Only backend serializer specs were added (`user_serializer_spec.rb`) to assert JSON includes `:website_name`, but nothing in the diff adds/updates a frontend rendering test to ensure the template correctly gates on `model.website_name` and renders the expected link attributes (`href`, `rel` via `removeNoFollow`, `target`). Serializer specs alone would not catch a mismatch in the template/property wiring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `websiteName` computed property is deleted from the user controller, but there is no evidence existing QUnit/acceptance tests referencing it or the profile website display were updated or removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* update the profile website display: `user/user.hbs` switches from `websiteName` to `model.website_name`, and the controller computed `websiteName` is removed accordingly. It also adds/updates tests on the backend (`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb`) to cover the new `website_name` serializer logic. While the diff doesn’t show QUnit/acceptance tests, the finding’s claim that there’s “no evidence” the display was updated is directly contradicted by the template changes shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The degradation path where the serializer omits `website_name` and the website silently disappears from profiles has no acceptance test to catch the regression

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `website_name` is explicitly added to `UserSerializer`’s `untrusted_attributes` and is included whenever `website.present?` (`include_website_name`). A serializer spec is also added to cover `website_name` generation. The finding’s specific claim about a “degradation path where the serializer omits `website_name` and the website silently disappears” is not demonstrated by the shown changes: for a present website, the serializer will attempt to emit `website_name`, and the new tests cover the expected behavior. Lack of an *acceptance* test is not, by itself, a diff-grounded regression path here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies `website_name` is omitted/nil when `website` is blank; if `include_website_name` regressed to always-true, no test would fail

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `website_name` with conditional inclusion via `include_website_name` (returns `website.present?`). The spec only covers the "with filled out website" context and asserts `json[:website_name]` values there, but has no test ensuring `website_name` is omitted/nil when `website` is blank. If `include_website_name` regressed to always true, these tests wouldn’t catch the unwanted field on blank-website users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies `website_name` returns nil when `website` is present but unparseable (the `rescue nil` path), which serializes as `website_name: null` alongside a present `website`

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` with `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and `include_website_name` returning `website.present?`. That means if `website` is a non-empty but unparseable string, `website_name` will be included in the JSON (because `website.present?` is true) but will evaluate to nil and serialize as `website_name: null`. The added spec cases only cover valid URLs (`http://example.com/user`) and do not exercise the `rescue nil`/unparseable-path behavior, so the finding about a missing test for that edge case is accurate and specific to this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Path edge cases are unpinned: `URI('http://example.com').path` is `""` while `URI('http://example.com/').path` is `"/"`, so a same-domain website renders as `example.com` vs `example.com/` — a visible change from the old host-only display — and neither input is tested

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, same-domain (and some related) cases build the display string as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. Ruby’s `URI(...).path` differs for `http://example.com` ("" path) vs `http://example.com/` ("/" path), so the rendered `website_name` can be `example.com` vs `example.com/`. The old JS `websiteName` always showed host-only (`split("/")[2]`), so this introduces a visible inconsistency/edge case. The added specs cover `http://example.com/user` but do not test the empty-path vs root-slash inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Query strings/fragments (e.g. `?a=b`) are silently dropped from the displayed website name with no test documenting that intent

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the displayed name is built with `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` (or just `website_host`), which omits `URI(...).query` and `URI(...).fragment`. The specs added only cover host/path cases (e.g. `'http://example.com/user'`) and do not document whether dropping `?query` / `#fragment` from the displayed `website_name` is intended. The actual link `href` still uses `model.website`, so this is more a missing edge-case/intent test than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead conditional-inclusion guard: the new `include_website_name` method (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:154) is never invoked because ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8.x dispatches conditional attribute inclusion via `include_#{attribute}?` with a trailing question mark, so `website_name` is emitted unconditionally (as null for every user without a website); the new specs only serialize users with a website, so the suite passes whether the gate works or not and nothing in CI can detect the inert guard — the method should be renamed to `include_website_name?` and a spec added asserting the json has no `:website_name` key when the website is blank.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` as a serialized attribute (`untrusted_attributes` now includes `:website_name`) and defines an inclusion guard as `def include_website_name` (no trailing `?`). In typical ActiveModel::Serializer conditional inclusion, the hook is `include_<attr>?`; if that convention applies here, this guard will never be consulted and `website_name` will be serialized for all users (returning `nil` when `website` is blank due to `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`). The added specs only cover the case where `website` is present, so they would not catch the inert/misnamed guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `rescue nil` fallback at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:139 silently hides the website entirely for stored website values that strict URI parsing rejects (e.g. `http://example.com/my page`, URLs with non-ASCII characters or `|`): the old client-side code (`website.split("/")[2]`) still displayed the host for such values, but the new backend returns nil and the template's `{{#if model.website_name}}` renders nothing — a silent regression where the failure mode should be "show host", not "show nothing".

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` does `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and immediately `return if website_host.nil?`, so any stored `website` string that raises strict `URI(...)` parsing will yield `website_name == nil`. The template was changed from `{{#if websiteName}}` (client-side `website.split("/")[2]`) to `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so in those cases the website label/link will not render at all even though `website` is still present. The old logic would still show the host for many “invalid URI” strings like `http://example.com/my page`, making this a silent regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The domain-matching heuristic at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145-150 silently no-ops for common same-site cases: on a two-label instance domain (e.g. example.com), a website at `www.example.com/blog` or `blog.example.com/post` matches no branch (the elsif requires equal label counts, the else only matches when the website host is a dot-suffixed parent of the instance host), and sibling subdomains with differing label counts also fall through; additionally, the elsif branch — the most convoluted logic in the method — is the only branch with zero spec coverage, so future edits there are invisible to CI.

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch is newly added, relatively complex, and has no spec coverage in the diff (the added specs cover different-host, exact-host match, and "website is parent of instance" cases, but not the equal-label-count subdomain/sibling-subdomain scenario the `elsif` targets). The finding’s claim that `www.example.com` on an `example.com` instance "matches no branch" is imprecise (it hits the final `else` and returns just `website_host`), but the broader point about untested/non-obvious heuristic behavior for common subdomain cases is diff-grounded and actionable as a review concern rather than a provable defect.
